claims.statement: Covered equipment produces recurring, equipment-level recordkeeping rather than only a one-time certificate task.
Certification scope is expanding to specified alternative refrigerants, so a durable product must maintain rules beyond legacy F-gases.
There is a material Polish firm universe and an audit trigger: UDT reported more than 14,000 enterprise certificates and planned more than 3,400 inspections in 2024.
Enterprise certification is obtainable through UDT; no evidence establishes an unobtainable essential right for a documentation-software vendor.
The proposed core workflow is already sold in Poland at low prices, including a free substitute and 199-399 PLN monthly paid tiers.
The strongest plausible wedge is service-revenue recovery and lower-friction job closure, not compliance access alone.
CRO integration availability, channel willingness, paid conversion, churn, and support load are not established by public evidence.
No direct evidence establishes illegality, unobtainable essential rights, impossible conservative unit economics, or non-delegable founder incompatibility.

contrary_evidence: Montak directly matches much of the proposed workflow and publishes 0, 199, and 399 PLN monthly tiers.
Montero, Fieldworker, and Clima Pro provide additional direct Polish alternatives, including mobile protocols, F-gas records, equipment histories, and audit or CRO preparation.
The authoritative CRO and UDT rails remain available outside the product, limiting pricing power for compliance access.
The illustrative wealth path requires substantial share of a dated 14,000-plus certified-firm base or unvalidated European expansion.
